Subject: Follow-up & proposed A/B test plan — Redwood vs Hyperscaler (recap)

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

Recap:
- Primary goal: reduce inference cost while meeting p95 latency target of <= 120ms for user-facing generative assistant.
- Current baseline: Globex is evaluating Hyperscaler-A managed endpoints and considering a self-hosted stack.
- Success metrics: p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec sustained throughput, and end-to-end per-token cost.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) Run a controlled A/B benchmark comparing Redwood Hosted inference vs Hyperscaler-A API using your representative prompt set (attached test harness plan).
2) Focus metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec (sustained), and failure/retry rate.
3) We'll run identical traffic shapes (burst + steady) and share raw results + a summary deck.

I've attached a short A/B test plan (redwood-hyperscaler-abtest-plan.pdf) — it includes test scripts, payload shapes, and measurement definitions. Can you confirm: 
- test dataset (the 25 prompts you mentioned) is ok to use?
- do you want the runs in us-west region only?

If that looks good I can loop in Marcus (bench engineer) to schedule the runs and share credentials/machine details. Proposed window: Wed 03/03 or Thu 03/04 morning PST.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler A/B test results (raw + summary)

Hi all — ran the A/B tests this morning per plan. Attached are the raw CSV and a one-page summary. Key highlights below (all runs in us-west, pinned model family, steady-state window used for p95/p99):

Summary (steady-state, warmed cache):
- Redwood Hosted: p50=38ms, p95=92ms, p99=210ms; tokens/sec (sustained)=27.8
- Hyperscaler-A: p50=44ms, p95=168ms, p99=520ms; tokens/sec (sustained)=16.4
- Failed requests / retry rate: Redwood 0.8%, Hyperscaler-A 2.3% (retries mostly due to transient 5xx spikes during burst windows)
- Per-token cost (approx): Redwood $0.00095/token, Hyperscaler-A $0.00165/token (includes network egress estimate)

Notes/interpretation:
- Redwood shows materially lower p95 and much lower p99 in steady-state, with roughly 70% higher sustained tokens/sec on identical hardware profiles.
- Cold-start p95s are closer across both platforms; the main delta is under load bursts and tail behavior (our continuous batching + KV cache helps steady tail performance).

Attachments: abtest-p95-p99-results.csv, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-summary.pdf

Next steps I propose:
1) Review results with Globex infra team and validate measurement alignment (sequence length distribution, concurrency).
2) If results look good, we can propose a pilot (month-long dedicated capacity) that replicates production traffic for a quick operational validation.

Happy to jump on a quick 30m sync if folks want to walk through the CSV.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Bench Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
